# /crav1-explain-existing-system

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From the system notes](../../from-explain.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-explain-existing-system/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Read the system notes spark, ideas, intake, match, or existing-to-specs already wrote (docs/system/).

When system notes already exist, **[`/crav1-explain-existing-system`](crav1-explain-existing-system.md)** reads `docs/system/` and answers with a short TLDR. Longer goes one level deeper from the same notes. On every run it compares the feature index with each slice's diagram node and its line under `## How the parts connect`. Names match only by slug, spec title, or main resource name. It lists each slice missing entirely or partly, including done and retired, with status, and names [`/crav1-refresh-system-notes`](crav1-refresh-system-notes.md). It does not run it. When the picture has nothing on the question, it quotes the first paragraph of the matching spec, labelled as coming from the spec, and names [`/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`](crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this.md). When no spec matches either, it says so and names that skill. It is cross-cutting. It is not its own lane. It does not guess, write a second document, teach, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. It stays read-only.

Reads `docs/system/`. First answer is a short TLDR. Longer goes one level deeper from the same notes. The user can point it at one part, or ask whether the system can do something (yes and where, no, or not written down). When the picture has nothing on the question, quotes the matching spec's first paragraph, labelled as coming from the spec, and names [`/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`](crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this.md). When no spec matches either, says so and names that skill. Does not guess, write a second document, teach, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. On every run, lists each feature-index slice missing a diagram node or a connection line, including done and retired, with status, and names [`/crav1-refresh-system-notes`](crav1-refresh-system-notes.md).

## Runs when

System notes already exist. Called by the user.

## Reads

In short: `docs/system/` notes and the feature index.

Reads the `docs/system/` notes spark, ideas, intake, or match already wrote, and on every run the feature index against each slice’s node in `docs/system/diagrams.md` and its line in `## How the parts connect`.

## Writes

In short: Nothing (a short TLDR in chat).

Writes a short TLDR in the chat, one level deeper only when asked, one part when pointed at, and, when the picture has nothing on the question, the first paragraph of the matching spec labelled as coming from the spec. Shows a stale research note as stale.

## Does not

Leaves specs, code, and the picture alone.

Limits and exceptions: does not guess, invent a second document, teach, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. Names match only by slug, spec title, or main resource name. At the end it lists each slice missing entirely or partly, including done and retired, with status, and names [`/crav1-refresh-system-notes`](crav1-refresh-system-notes.md) without running it. When no spec matches either, it says so and names [`/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`](crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this.md) without running it. It does not clear a stale research mark.
